deviations: D1: ConsoleSmsSender registered unconditionally (not Development-only) via AuthFeatureConfiguration.AddFeatureDependencies. Reason: spec scope is 'SMS/push sending — interfaces only' so no production gateway exists in v1; env-gating would leave Production DI unresolvable. Documented decision: ConsoleSmsSender is the production implementation for v1; swap for a real gateway when the SMS provider contract is signed.

D2: User.DisplayName is set to the E.164 phone number on first-time customer creation. Reason: User.DisplayName is required (non-nullable) and there is no name collected during SMS auth. The E.164 phone is stable and parseable; customers can update their display name in a later profile endpoint.

D3: Rate-limit query shape uses ExpiresAt arithmetic rather than a CreatedAt column. SmsCode entity has no CreatedAt field (WI-03 field list is exhaustive: Id, Phone, CodeHash, ExpiresAt, Attempts, UsedAt). Since all codes use a fixed 5-minute lifetime (CodeLifetime constant), creation time is exactly ExpiresAt - CodeLifetime. The rate-limit threshold queries therefore translate: 'created within N minutes' becomes 'ExpiresAt > now - N minutes + CodeLifetime'. Both limits (10-min window, 60-s gap) use this derivation. Count includes all codes regardless of UsedAt or Attempts — expired/used codes still count toward the limit.

D4: RequestCode_FourthWithin10Min_Returns429 advances FakeTimeProvider by 61 seconds between each of the 3 allowed sends so the 60-s gap gate passes while all 3 prior codes still have ExpiresAt within the 10-minute window. Without the 61-second advances, the second send would 429 via the 60-s rule and the 3-per-10-min rule would never be exercised.

D5: Tests achieve isolation by using a unique random phone per test (UniquePhone() helper) rather than DB reset. Rate limits are per-phone, so a reused phone across concurrent test runs would cause flaky 429s. The shared PostgresFixture has no ResetDatabaseAsync; the per-phone isolation pattern mirrors WI-05's per-slug isolation.

D6: RED was a single batch compile-error red for all six integration tests; per-behavior RED/GREEN cycles were not run individually. Each error path (429 x2, 401 x3) was exercised in the green run and confirmed by the specific status code assertions passing. Validator tests were written individually with a compile-error RED (missing FluentValidation.TestHelper namespace) before GREEN.

D7: AddError(propertyExpr, message, errorCode) — the FastEndpoints overload places errorMessage second and errorCode third. All handler-side AddError calls updated to pass a human-readable message string and the error code constant as the third argument, so localization keys land in the code field rather than the message field.

D8: Common/PhoneNormalizer.cs is sanctioned shared infrastructure under rules/architecture.md#common-infrastructure (reused by RequestCodeEndpoint and VerifyCodeEndpoint). Placed in Common/ ahead of WI-08 which will also require phone normalization for customer lookups.

D9: Micro-fix pass (impl-reviewer F1–F5). F2: Attempts increment made atomic via ExecuteUpdateAsync with WHERE Attempts < MaxAttempts guard — eliminates race-condition cap bypass. F4: Success path consolidated to single SaveChangesAsync covering UsedAt + user upsert + refresh token — atomicity via implicit EF transaction; AsNoTracking removed from existing-user lookup so LastLoginAt is set on the tracked entity. F5: Wrong-code tests (VerifyCode_WrongCode_Returns401 and VerifyCode_FiveWrongAttempts_InvalidatesCode) now derive wrong code by flipping last digit of real code instead of hardcoding 000000 — eliminates 10^-6 flake. F1: docs/specs/in-progress/backend-core-work-items.md §WI-06 error-paths line updated to uniform 401 with no body. F3: PhoneNormalizer already in files_changed; this deviation records the sanctioned-infrastructure rationale.
notes: E.164 normalization rules: (1) input stripped of spaces and dashes; (2) if result matches +[7-15 digits] → accepted as-is; (3) if result is exactly 9 digits → prefixed with +420 (Czech default); (4) anything else → rejected with PhoneInvalid. Implemented in Common/PhoneNormalizer.TryNormalize used by both validators and both endpoints (single shared helper prevents normalize-in-request-code / not-in-verify-code lookup miss). Code generation: RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(0, 1_000_000).ToString('D6') gives a 6-digit zero-padded string. Hash scheme: SHA-256 hex (lowercase) of the UTF-8 bytes of the raw code string — same pattern as JwtIssuer.HashRefreshToken but in a private static method on each endpoint (not added to JwtIssuer to avoid semantic coupling). Rate-limit query shape documented in D3. ConsoleSmsSender logs only the last-4-masked phone and never the message body (which contains the OTP), satisfying logging#what-must-not-appear-in-logs. ISmsSender registered as Singleton in AuthFeatureConfiguration since the recording fake in tests is replaced per-factory via ConfigureTestServices. VerifyCode dead-code check: smsCode.Attempts >= 5 is evaluated BEFORE the hash comparison so 5-wrong-then-correct returns 401 as required. On every wrong attempt, Attempts is incremented and saved before returning 401. JwtIssuer.IssueAccessToken(user, fleetSlug: null) correctly omits fleet_id and fleet_slug claims for customers since those fields are null. RefreshToken row creation mirrors StaffLoginEndpoint pattern verbatim. User.LastLoginAt is updated on second+ logins via ExecuteUpdateAsync to avoid loading the full entity. SmsCode.UsedAt is set on correct-code consumption to prevent replay; UsedAt=null filter in VerifyCode query ensures only fresh codes are found. VerifyCodeEndpoint user read query uses AsNoTracking() per ef-core#asnotracking (read-only lookup before Add or ExecuteUpdateAsync). FluentValidation.TestHelper is included in FluentValidation 12.x via the FluentValidation.TestHelper namespace (no separate package).
